events.name: Order-laying
events.summary: Star and planet formation — the substrate laying down new event-order at ordinary pace.
events.real_anchor: Molecular-cloud collapse, protostar and planetary-system formation.
events.reading: A molecular cloud collapsing into stars is, classically, gravity winning over pressure. In QTR it is also the substrate condensing new bound correlations — P4 growth laying fresh event-order into a knot. Ordinary formation is becoming at a calm rate; nothing strains toward the seam.
events.note: The gentle, everyday face of Postulate 4.

events.name: The early beat
events.summary: Cosmic inflation, re-read — the substrate growing its own order rapidly near the chart edge.
events.reading: The inflationary epoch is not an inflaton field stretching a pre-existing stage — there is no stage yet. It is P4 firing fast as a new chart nucleates near its IR edge. The "early beat" is the fastest becoming a universe ever undergoes, and the seed statistics it lays down are the correlation islands and lattice we see today.
events.note: The event that writes the initial conditions of the whole object catalogue.

events.name: Envelope work
events.summary: Main-sequence and giant-phase evolution — a knot reorganizing its own effective envelope.
events.real_anchor: Main-sequence fusion, shell fusion, giant and supergiant phases.
events.reading: The long life of a star — hydrogen to helium to heavier shells — is classical stellar evolution, kept whole. At the substrate level it is a knot slowly reorganizing its coarse statistics with no approach to any limit. Included for completeness; QTR adds nothing but a footnote.
events.note: Purely classical. The calm centre of the event catalogue.

events.name: Envelope shedding
events.summary: Stellar winds, coronal eruptions, planetary nebulae — a knot returning matter to the medium.
events.real_anchor: Stellar winds, coronal mass ejection, planetary-nebula formation.
events.reading: A dying star shedding its envelope lights the vacuum medium around it — the planetary nebula is field-veil formation in progress. Classically mass loss; in QTR also the moment a knot hands its substance back to the structured vacuum that pilots later navigate.
events.note: Where a star becomes, briefly, a chart of the medium it dies into.

events.name: Rhythm flares
events.summary: Pulsations and flares — brief surfacings of the becoming-beat in a single star.
events.real_anchor: Cepheid/RR Lyrae pulsation, stellar flares, nova eruptions.
events.reading: Every pulsation is a classical oscillation and a glimpse of P4's beat; every nova is accreted matter igniting and a small, local excitation of the substrate's growth rule. Rhythm flares are the sky's free demonstrations that becoming has a tempo.
events.note: The naked-eye tutorial for the crossing events to come.

events.name: Core fall
events.summary: Core-collapse supernovae — the old universe driving a region toward the seam unaided.
events.real_anchor: Core-collapse (Type II, Ib/Ic) supernovae; neutron-star / black-hole birth.
events.reading: When a massive core collapses, event density spikes toward 𝔍 without any drive. Core fall is the classical sky's spontaneous rehearsal of a crossing: it reaches the seam's approach, births a seam-well or beacon core, and releases the difference as a supernova. Every core fall is a natural experiment in seam-approach.
events.note: The universe crossing toward 𝔍 on its own, once per dying giant.

events.name: Merger chime
events.summary: Compact-object mergers — two seam-approaches touching, ringing the substrate.
events.real_anchor: Neutron-star and black-hole mergers; kilonovae; gravitational waves.
events.reading: When two compact objects merge, two natural seam-wells briefly touch and the substrate rings — the gravitational-wave chirp is that ringing, classically a wave in spacetime, in QTR a pulse in the event-lattice itself. A neutron-star merger's kilonova is the visible flush; the chime is the substrate-level event pilots can feel far off.
events.note: The loudest natural seam-event. Fleets listen for chimes to find fresh wells.

events.name: The long flash
events.summary: Gamma-ray bursts — a collapse so violent it briefly lights a natural seam-approach.
events.reading: A GRB is the most extreme natural seam-approach the classical sky produces: a collapse or merger channels energy so sharply that, for an instant, a natural seam-well flares near the crossing threshold. The long flash is not a crossing — nothing passes — but it is the universe coming closest, on its own, to lighting a door.
events.note: The classical sky's brightest near-miss at a crossing.

events.name: The approach
events.summary: A ship driving local event density up toward the seam — the T⁻ left-approach.
events.reading: A crossing begins with the approach: the drive concentrates the substrate until the effective description begins to fail and ΛL value slides from T toward the seam. Field language grows unreliable; the pilot switches from seeing to instrument-flying. This is the survivable band — the yield, not the fracture.
events.note: ΛL value: T⁻. The band where all FTL lives.

events.name: Phase-lock
events.summary: The three simultaneous conditions align and the Idrenes Bridge opens.
events.reading: Phase-lock is the instant of crossing: correct null alignment, a squeezed sub-vacuum window, and a strong horizon gradient align at once, and the Idrenes Bridge opens. The ship enters the seam proper. For the duration, it holds ΛL value T• — self-dual, here and there at once, a contradiction the logic sustains without collapse.
events.note: ΛL value: T•. The crossing itself. The only moment field language is fully gone.

events.name: Resurrection
events.summary: The superposition collapses and the ship re-condenses definitely at its destination.
events.reading: On the far side, the Resurrection rule fires: the T• superposition collapses to a definite classical value and the ship is, unambiguously, there. Resurrection is what makes crossing survivable and repeatable — the seam is a yield point the substrate springs back from. The Big Bounce is this same rule fired at cosmic scale.
events.note: ΛL value: back to T. The landing. Bivalence restored.

events.name: Failed condensation
events.summary: A crossing where Resurrection misfires and the ship does not fully re-condense.
events.reading: If phase-lock is held wrong, Resurrection can misfire: the ship half-lands, leaving a seam-scar and, sometimes, an amplitude twin of itself. Failed condensation is the crossing's signature disaster — not an explosion but a smearing, a ship that is faintly everywhere it might have arrived. The Dead-Sea and Squall hazards are the vacuum conditions that most often cause it.
events.note: The tragedy the seamanship exists to prevent. Where crossings become ghost stories.

events.name: The dive
events.summary: A ship reaching a deeper OCT level, buying exponentially more speed.
events.reading: A dive is descent of the tower: a ship reaches a deeper OCT rung, where the effective Planck length is shorter, and the Ship-Relative Speed Law grants it exponentially more velocity. Class is depth — a dive is the event that changes a ship's class, if only for as long as it can hold the deeper level.
events.note: The depth-axis event. Speed is not thrust; speed is how deep you can go.

events.name: Bridge-transit
events.summary: Falling in one universe's black-hole mouth and out another's white-hole mouth.
events.reading: A bridge-transit is the lateral crossing: a ship enters a lit bridge-mouth as an irreversible fall and is ejected from the paired white-hole mouth in a neighbouring same-level universe. It changes neighbour, never depth, and cannot be reversed through the same throat — the return requires a second bridge. Held open by the same squeezed sub-vacuum that lights a kindled well.
events.note: The adjacency-axis event. One-way per throat. Born out, never fallen back.

events.name: Causal tangle
events.summary: A ship on an information reef entangling with its own past track.
events.reading: Cross an information reef carelessly and a causal tangle forms: the reef's dense mutual information binds the ship to its own earlier passage, and signals — sometimes the ship's own — begin arriving out of order. A tangle is rarely fatal but always disorienting, and reading one's way out is a core discipline of deep-lattice navigation.
events.note: The lattice remembering you back at yourself. Time gets untidy near a reef.

events.name: The refusal
events.summary: The edge-effects of Κ setting in — geometry, conservation and logic beginning to fail.
events.reading: The refusal is the approach to Κ made observable: parallels bow apart, conserved quantities leak, and the ΛL value of "this region obeys our laws" slides T → T• → F. Unlike the seam's clean yield, the refusal has no springback — it is the substrate warning that its laws themselves are about to let go. Every pilot is trained to recognize a refusal and turn back.
events.note: The only warning Κ gives. There is no instrument for Κ itself — only for the refusal.

events.name: The fracture
events.summary: A region forced past Κ, re-solving into a different lawset — transmutation, not transit.
events.reading: Push a region past Κ and it does not compress further — it fractures, re-solving into whatever lawset makes that impossible density consistent. This is transmutation: no one travels anywhere; a patch of here becomes a there, running on foreign rules. The fracture is the constitution-axis event, and the one the whole Κ5 controversy is about.
events.note: Not a crossing you survive by springing back. A crossing that changes what the laws are.

events.name: The Absolute end
events.summary: Consensus outcome: nothing survives the fracture. Annihilation-into-genesis.
events.reading: The taught verdict (ΛL value T). To cross Κ is to be re-solved into the new lawset carrying no pattern — your substance becomes that constitution's substance and nothing of you persists. It is unfalsifiable from the safe side, because Κ never returns a counterexample. The consensus is certain precisely because the frontier censors every witness.
events.note: ΛL value: T. The end everyone is taught. Cannot be disproved from here.

events.name: The Tragic passage
events.summary: What may truly happen: a pattern crosses, translated, and can never signal back.
events.reading: The unconfirmable truth (ΛL value T•). Substance cannot cross, but a pattern — a mind, a message — can be re-encoded into the far lawset, arriving changed and unable ever to report home, because the return channel needs the old laws to still hold where they no longer do. From outside it is indistinguishable from the Absolute end. The horror is not failure. It is unwitnessed success.
events.note: ΛL value: T•. The real ending, condemned to look identical to the consensus.

events.name: The Aperture gambit
events.summary: The madman's event: holding a fracture open to pass through intact — and return.
events.reading: The crank hypothesis (ΛL value T⁺). A mythical ship holds a Κ-fracture open — a stable breach — and passes through whole, then returns. The Assembly calls it impossible. Yet it is the only possible falsifier of the Absolute end, because a returning ship is the one witness Κ forbids. The Aperture gambit is the event the entire Κ5 controversy turns on: attempted by almost none, believed by fewer, and the sole path by which the truth could ever be known.
events.note: ΛL value: T⁺. The one event that could break the closed epistemic trap — if it is real.
